Every Configuration A (TUB) line is dropped from this room, and the Configuration B lines are the ones to build - they are no longer carried as an open conflict on this key. WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT CLOSE IS THE DRAWINGS, and that is the architect's to close, not the crew's: A100 and G001 both still mark room 118 "T" (tub), and conflicts.md A11 and B4.4 are still formally OPEN on it. data/project.sqlite records the open part this way, verbatim: "A11 verbatim: "Do not order the 438 bath package off either matrix." C-01 verbatim: "The four architectural types drawn with a roll-in cover all seven accessible keys ... G100.2 provides two. Those cannot both be true." Only Austin can close this." Nobody should order a bath package off either matrix, and the architect still owes a corrected A100 / G001, until A11 and B4.4 are closed.

0da06fc3d565.instanceNote: DB GAP — no row exists, and this is the single most transferable finding on the walk. The requirement is PRINTED: M101 GN7 requires min 12"x12" access in ceilings/walls to valves, traps, dampers, cleanouts and controls; M301 Key Note 4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC unit maintenance; M101 GN31/GN32 require approved access with a permanent exterior label reading FIRE DAMPER in letters at least 0.5" high. But the PLACEMENT is missing — none of the ten A550-A556 guestroom RCPs draws an access panel, including A555 view 02, which governs this room and whose keynotes are 18, 19, 7, 4, 1. The only flush-access-panel keynote anywhere in the A12x/A55x set is keynote 5 (verbatim: 'FLUSH ACCESS PANEL WITH DROP IN DOOR - MFR. ISC STYLE MARK MO.#CAP-1818 - CONFIRM SIZE WITH ENGINEER OF RECORD - TEXTURE & PAINT TO MATCH ADJACENT CEILING'), and it is placed ONLY at the ICE-MACHINE alcove — on A121 (239), A122 (339) and A123 (439). CORRECTED: the draft named A121 alone; it is on three sheets, and A120 carries the note in its list but places it nowhere on floor 1, so floor 1 has no keyed access panel at all. This is a real, repeating, 115-room omission, an RFI candidate and a CO-inspection exposure — an inspector cannot verify a damper he cannot reach. Not invented: the requirement is printed, only the placement is missing. CORRECTED FROM THE DRAFT: the label requirement is M101 GN31/GN32, not M501. Whatever room 101 shows, expect it in all 16 and on floors 2-4.
0da06fc3d565.label: Access panel in the bath ceiling to the fire damper and volume damper, min 12"x12", with permanent damper label
0da06fc3d565.src: M101 GN7; M301 Key Note 4; M101 GN31/GN32 (permanent 0.5" label); against A555 view 02 (keynotes 18, 19, 7, 4, 1 — no access panel) and the other nine A550-A556 RCPs
0da06fc3d565.verifyAtPunch: Look at the bath ceiling and record 'access panel present, size ___, labelled ___' or 'ABSENT'; if absent photograph the intact lid and log it as an RFI item. Cut nothing.

121591af18d1.instanceNote: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE READINGS — THE QUANTITY MAY BE 1 OR ZERO. M201 schedules EF-1 as a real Panasonic ceiling fan (remarks 1 brick vent, 2 ceiling radiation damper, 3 'switch w/ room lights', 5 backdraft damper, 6 off-white aluminium grille, 9 UL/Energy Star/AMCA); M202 and M301-M304 repeat it. But M305's riser diagrams show each guestroom inlet as a PLAIN CEILING GRILLE + Aldes regulator on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8 to EF-11 — no in-room fan anywhere. A grille-only inlet and a dedicated in-room fan cannot both be true. Supporting but not conclusive: E400's Panel A/B guestroom schedules carry NO exhaust-fan circuit (though remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit and need no breaker). coordination_issues C-06 — a 115-unit buy. DO NOT order 115 Panasonic on this. SECOND, SEPARATE TWO-READING CONFLICT ON THE SWITCHING, both carried: M201 remark 3 says the fan is switched WITH the room lights; G402's guestroom-bath general note 3 says verbatim 'CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT'. 121591af18d1.verifyAtPunch: Drop the bath grille and look — record 'fan housing' or 'bare duct to riser', with a photo. Then flip the bath light switch and record whether the fan runs with the light or on a separate switch. That single observation closes C-06.

24bab0002794.instanceNote: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT OPERATING TEST IN THIS BATHROOM. Guestroom HWS is distributed at 120 F per P202/P305 and there is NO guestroom thermostatic mixing valve scheduled — P301/P305's 110 F TMV note is scoped to PUBLIC lavatories and hand sinks — so this pressure-balancing valve is the ONLY temperature protection at the shower. A530 keyed note 14 reads verbatim 'ON/OFF - PRESSURE BALANCING VALVE' and is placed on views 04 and 05. Confirm it is a pressure-balancing valve, not a plain mixer. No control height is dimensioned on A530 for the standard rooms (the 8"-10" band and MAX dims belong to the accessible sheets A532/A532.1 and do not apply here).
24bab0002794.label: On/off PRESSURE-BALANCING (anti-scald) valve - P104 gives the guestroom rows SH-3 / SH-4 only 'Delta T24859 supply'; NO valve or cartridge model is printed for the guestroom
24bab0002794.src: A530 keyed note 14 (placed on views 04 and 05); P104 REMARKS rows SH-3/SH-4; P202/P305 (120 F HWS distribution); P301/P305 (TMV scoped to public lavs)
24bab0002794.verifyAtPunch: Run the shower at a comfortable setting, then flush the toilet in the same room while it runs — the shower temperature must not spike; then run the lavatory hot and confirm the same. Confirm the trim is the pressure-balancing model, not a plain mixer.

TREAT THE SUBSTITUTION AS NOT APPROVED: the American Standard sheet offers THREE models with NONE ticked, the Moen sheet offers TWO with NEITHER ticked, and there is no transmittal and no stamp. c93e819f19c0.instanceNote: DOWNGRADED FROM THE DRAFT'S HIGH — THE COUNT IS DERIVED, NOT READ, FOR THIS ROOM TYPE. The arithmetic is sound: FA-1 schedules 121 x SKPHOTOW + 121 x B200S-LF-WH, which reconciles exactly to 115 keys + the 6 second detectors in the 6 one-bedroom units, and A100's matrix puts no one-bedroom on floor 1 — so 1 per key on this floor is well argued. But packages/fire-appliance.md rates the row covering QQ Wide Connecting at MEDIUM and states in terms that it was NOT read off FA-2/FA-3 for these types; the 303/305/307/311 and 304/306/308 verifications are OTHER room types. Well-argued arithmetic is MEDIUM, not HIGH — the same extraction gap flagged loudly for sprinklers on this exact room. THE LOW-FREQUENCY SOUNDER BASE IS THE AUDIBLE APPLIANCE FOR THIS SLEEPING ROOM — a corridor horn does not satisfy it. FA-1's audibility chart: sleeping rooms ambient 35 dBA, design 75 dBA, low frequency, visual required. (Note E500 FA note 17's 15-dBA-over-ambient criterion would give only 50 dBA; the submittal is more onerous and governs — test to 75.) Each detector carries TWO addresses on FA-2/FA-3, an SLC address and a NAC/power-supply circuit — get both read back at the panel. E500 FA note 10 requires emergency-system junction boxes and cover plates to be PAINTED RED; any exposed FA plate in this finished room is red or it is a punch item. SETTLES IT: read the FA-2 first-floor region for 101 — the same document-reading task that closes the sprinkler row.

009c6d7c50f8.instanceNote: MISSING FROM THE DRAFT — and it is the first device anyone touches in the room. A600's door schedule puts GR-1 ENTRY on hardware set 1, and Set #1 reads verbatim: "Guestroom Entry Door — 1 One Way Viewer ((2) @ Accessible Rooms); 1 Privacy Latch; 1 Door Sweep; 1 Vinyl Threshold; 1 Perimeter Gasketing; 1 Door Closer - w/ 90° Stop; 1 Advance Card Lock; 1.5 PR Hinges". 105 is NOT accessible, so ONE one-way viewer here, not two. TWO THINGS OPEN. (1) SCOPE — NEEDS A RULING FROM AUSTIN, stated rather than decided: it comes off A600 (doors and hardware), not the E-series, so it can be argued onto the door/hardware punch instead of this one; against that, it is an electronic device the walker operates on this walk, no other list in this room set is carrying it, and _trade-truth.json extracted it under Low Voltage with the same open ruling. Put it in ONE place — do not let it fall between the two. (2) PRODUCT — A600 gives no manufacturer, no model, and does not say whether the lock is standalone-battery or networked, so there is nothing to punch the hardware against beyond presence and function; A600's own flags record that whether a set's Advance Cardlock is the guest-facing lock is implied by the room, not stated. SETTLES IT: the approved door-hardware submittal and the lock vendor's programming/keying schedule.

n_config.text: BATHING CONFIGURATION - RULED, WITH ONE THING STILL OPEN. Austin ruling D19 (the owner, asked directly on 2026-08-20): room 118 is built to Configuration B, the ROLL-IN SHOWER. Every Configuration A (TUB) line is dropped from this room, and the Configuration B lines are the ones to build - they are no longer carried as an open conflict on this key. WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT CLOSE IS THE DRAWINGS, and that is the architect's to close, not the crew's: A100 and G001 both still mark room 118 "T" (tub), and conflicts.md A11 and B4.4 are still formally OPEN on it. data/project.sqlite records the open part this way, verbatim: "A11 verbatim: "Do not order the 438 bath package off either matrix." C-01 verbatim: "The four architectural types drawn with a roll-in cover all seven accessible keys ... G100.2 provides two. Those cannot both be true." Only Austin can close this." The ruling supersedes the tub mark for construction. It does not correct the drawings. Nobody should order a bath package off either matrix, and the architect still owes a corrected A100 / G001, until A11 and B4.4 are closed.

0da06fc3d565.instanceNote: DB GAP — no row exists, and this is the single most transferable finding on the walk. The requirement is PRINTED: M101 GN7 requires min 12"x12" access in ceilings/walls to valves, traps, dampers, cleanouts and controls; M301 Key Note 4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC unit maintenance; M101 GN31/GN32 require approved access with a permanent exterior label reading FIRE DAMPER in letters at least 0.5" high. But the PLACEMENT is missing — none of the ten A550-A556 guestroom RCPs draws an access panel, including A555 view 02, which governs this room and whose keynotes are 18, 19, 7, 4, 1. The only flush-access-panel keynote anywhere in the A12x/A55x set is keynote 5 (verbatim: 'FLUSH ACCESS PANEL WITH DROP IN DOOR - MFR. ISC STYLE MARK MO.#CAP-1818 - CONFIRM SIZE WITH ENGINEER OF RECORD - TEXTURE & PAINT TO MATCH ADJACENT CEILING'), and it is placed ONLY at the ICE-MACHINE alcove — on A121 (239), A122 (339) and A123 (439). CORRECTED: the draft named A121 alone; it is on three sheets, and A120 carries the note in its list but places it nowhere on floor 1, so floor 1 has no keyed access panel at all. This is a real, repeating, 115-room omission, an RFI candidate and a CO-inspection exposure — an inspector cannot verify a damper he cannot reach. Not invented: the requirement is printed, only the placement is missing. CORRECTED FROM THE DRAFT: the label requirement is M101 GN31/GN32, not M501. Whatever room 101 shows, expect it in all 16 and on floors 2-4.
0da06fc3d565.label: Access panel in the bath ceiling to the fire damper and volume damper, min 12"x12", with permanent damper label
0da06fc3d565.src: M101 GN7; M301 Key Note 4; M101 GN31/GN32 (permanent 0.5" label); against A555 view 02 (keynotes 18, 19, 7, 4, 1 — no access panel) and the other nine A550-A556 RCPs
0da06fc3d565.verifyAtPunch: Look at the bath ceiling and record 'access panel present, size ___, labelled ___' or 'ABSENT'; if absent photograph the intact lid and log it as an RFI item. Cut nothing.
0da06fc3d565.where: Bathroom ceiling, 7'-3" PT-07 painted gyp lid, at the FD/VD above it

121591af18d1.instanceNote: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE READINGS — THE QUANTITY MAY BE 1 OR ZERO. M201 schedules EF-1 as a real Panasonic ceiling fan (remarks 1 brick vent, 2 ceiling radiation damper, 3 'switch w/ room lights', 5 backdraft damper, 6 off-white aluminium grille, 9 UL/Energy Star/AMCA); M202 and M301-M304 repeat it. But M305's riser diagrams show each guestroom inlet as a PLAIN CEILING GRILLE + Aldes regulator on a central riser driven by roof fans EF-8 to EF-11 — no in-room fan anywhere. A grille-only inlet and a dedicated in-room fan cannot both be true. Supporting but not conclusive: E400's Panel A/B guestroom schedules carry NO exhaust-fan circuit (though remark 3 would put a fan on the Lighting circuit and need no breaker). coordination_issues C-06 — a 115-unit buy. DO NOT order 115 Panasonic on this. SECOND, SEPARATE TWO-READING CONFLICT ON THE SWITCHING, both carried: M201 remark 3 says the fan is switched WITH the room lights; G402's guestroom-bath general note 3 says verbatim 'CEILING MOUNTED LIGHT FIXTURE AND FAN TO BE SWITCHED SEPARATELY FROM LIGHT'. Record which way it is wired; do not write either up. SETTLES IT FASTEST: this walk — look behind the grille in this room.

121591af18d1.verifyAtPunch: Drop the bath grille and look — record 'fan housing' or 'bare duct to riser', with a photo. Then flip the bath light switch and record whether the fan runs with the light or on a separate switch. That single observation closes C-06.

AGAINST: P402 places the floor drain in ACCESSIBLE UNITS. FOR — AND THERE ARE NOW TWO SOURCES, CORRECTED FROM THE DRAFT: (1) A530 keyed note 20 ('FLOOR DRAIN LOCATION - MAINTAIN ACCESSIBLE COMPLIANT SLOPES TO DRAIN') is PLACED on plan 01, the standard guest-bath plan that serves all 15 non-accessible first-floor rooms including 101; (2) E400 General Note 4, printed on the typical-guestroom sheet governing all six enlarged plans including 'QQ Studio (Detail 05) — Panel A', requires 'Slope floors to drain; slope <= 1:48 any direction' — a slope-to-drain requirement on the standard plan presupposes a drain on the standard plan. G402 bath general note 4 repeats it. That does not close the conflict, but the FOR side has two sources, not one. Separately: THE GUESTROOM FLOOR DRAIN HAS NO MARK AND NO SCHEDULED PRODUCT — P104's Drain and Drainage Appurtenance Schedule carries FD-1 (Mech/Laundry, Zurn Z550), FD-2 (Unfinished, Zurn Z415B) and FD-3 (Funnel, Zurn Z514E), none of which is a guestroom drain, so no make, model or strainer finish is specified for the item the walker is standing over. 009c6d7c50f8.instanceNote: MISSING FROM THE DRAFT — and it is the first device anyone touches in the room. A600's door schedule puts GR-1 ENTRY on hardware set 1, and Set #1 reads verbatim: "Guestroom Entry Door — 1 One Way Viewer ((2) @ Accessible Rooms); 1 Privacy Latch; 1 Door Sweep; 1 Vinyl Threshold; 1 Perimeter Gasketing; 1 Door Closer - w/ 90° Stop; 1 Advance Card Lock; 1.5 PR Hinges". 105 is NOT accessible, so ONE one-way viewer here, not two. TWO THINGS OPEN. (1) SCOPE — NEEDS A RULING FROM AUSTIN, stated rather than decided: it comes off A600 (doors and hardware), not the E-series, so it can be argued onto the door/hardware punch instead of this one; against that, it is an electronic device the walker operates on this walk, no other list in this room set is carrying it, and _trade-truth.json extracted it under Low Voltage with the same open ruling. Put it in ONE place — do not let it fall between the two. (2) PRODUCT — A600 gives no manufacturer, no model, and does not say whether the lock is standalone-battery or networked, so there is nothing to punch the hardware against beyond presence and function; A600's own flags record that whether a set's Advance Cardlock is the guest-facing lock is implied by the room, not stated. SETTLES IT: the approved door-hardware submittal and the lock vendor's programming/keying schedule.

The requirement is PRINTED — M101 N7 requires min 12"x12" access to valves, traps, dampers, cleanouts and controls; M301 Key Note 4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC maintenance; M101 N31/N32 require approved access with a permanent exterior label in letters at least 1/2" high reading FIRE DAMPER. But the PLACEMENT is missing: none of the ten A550–A556 guestroom RCPs draws one, and A555 view 02's placed keynotes are only 18, 19, 7, 4 and 1. The only flush-access-panel keynote anywhere in the A12x/A55x set is A121 keynote 5, at the ICE-MACHINE alcove. 0da06fc3d565.instanceNote: DB GAP — no row exists, and this is the single most transferable finding on the walk. The requirement is PRINTED: M101 GN7 requires min 12"x12" access in ceilings/walls to valves, traps, dampers, cleanouts and controls; M301 Key Note 4 requires an access panel above the ceiling for HVAC unit maintenance; M101 GN31/GN32 require approved access with a permanent exterior label reading FIRE DAMPER in letters at least 0.5" high. But the PLACEMENT is missing — none of the ten A550-A556 guestroom RCPs draws an access panel, including A555 view 02, which governs this room and whose keynotes are 18, 19, 7, 4, 1. The only flush-access-panel keynote anywhere in the A12x/A55x set is keynote 5 (verbatim: 'FLUSH ACCESS PANEL WITH DROP IN DOOR - MFR. ISC STYLE MARK MO.#CAP-1818 - CONFIRM SIZE WITH ENGINEER OF RECORD - TEXTURE & PAINT TO MATCH ADJACENT CEILING'), and it is placed ONLY at the ICE-MACHINE alcove — on A121 (239), A122 (339) and A123 (439). CORRECTED: the draft named A121 alone; it is on three sheets, and A120 carries the note in its list but places it nowhere on floor 1, so floor 1 has no keyed access panel at all. That 3-hole reading was an inference imported from packages/fire-appliance.md §4.2, not a statement on a sheet, and a walker following it would have written up correctly-installed faucets in every room he entered. ISC STYLE MARK MO.#CAP-1818 - CONFIRM SIZE WITH ENGINEER OF RECORD - TEXTURE & PAINT TO MATCH ADJACENT CEILING'), and it is placed ONLY at the ICE-MACHINE alcove — on A121 (239), A122 (339) and A123 (439). WHY 3 IS A WORSE GUESS HERE: 101 is QQ WIDE — A555 dimensions it 13'-10" / 12'-11 3/8" CLEAR against the standard QQ's 12'-8" / 12'-0", and G001 prints 535 sqft vs 480. OV-001 rules that ITEM counts do not change for the Wide variant, but sprinkler spacing is AREA-driven and FP-1 is a separate shop drawing, not A555 — OV-001 does not cover it. a141d66a3655.instanceNote: NO DECK HOLE COUNT IS STATED ON ANY SHEET — CORRECTED, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HAVE COST THE MOST. The draft made the hole count the pass/fail discriminator ('3 = as designed, 1 = the substitution') on the claim that P104's Delta 581LF is a 3-hole trim. P104 says no such thing. What P104's REMARKS column prints, verbatim on rows L-3 and L-4, is: 'Faucet Delta 581LF-GPM-PP manual 1.0 GPM, less 3-hole escutcheon'. 'Less' means supplied WITHOUT the 3-hole escutcheon — the deck plate that lets a single-hole faucet cover a 3-hole deck is DELETED — which reads toward a SINGLE-hole install, the opposite of the draft's claim. That 3-hole reading was an inference imported from packages/fire-appliance.md §4.2, not a statement on a sheet, and a walker following it would have written up correctly-installed faucets in every room he entered. RECORD the make, model and hole count as DATA. DO NOT JUDGE EITHER.

fe528f002e3e.instanceNote: EXPECTED QUANTITY IS ZERO — qty 1 means one CHECK performed once, not one installed item. Emitted as a line rather than folded away so the crew physically has the reject in front of them. THE ROW OF RECORD IS P104: Decolav Callensia 1402-CWH + Delta 581LF-GPM-PP. TREAT THE SUBSTITUTION AS NOT APPROVED: the American Standard sheet offers THREE models with NONE ticked, the Moen sheet offers TWO with NEITHER ticked, and there is no transmittal and no stamp. Under the precedence chain (user override > submittal > drawing > spec) a catalogue page with no selection and no stamp is not a submittal, so it does not enter the chain and supersedes nothing. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE MAKE, NOT THE HOLE COUNT — CORRECTED. The draft told the walker to stop on a single-hole deck; no sheet states a deck hole count, so hole count proves nothing. What proves it is the BRANDING: an American Standard Studio bowl or a Moen M-Dura faucet in place of the Decolav Callensia bowl and the Delta 581LF. If the AS/Moen set is ever ticked and stamped it WILL supersede P104 and change the countertop cutout on 115 vanity tops — which is why the make matters.
